title: Pressure-Cooked Chicken & Veg Stock
description: Super collagen-rich chicken and vegetable stock made with feet and necks, aromatic vegetables, herbs, and warm spices. Delicious on its own or as a base for other cooking.

notes: Reference only: these are Roli Roti chicken bone broth label values applied to a 96 fl oz batch (12 cups), not measured nutrition for this homemade stock. The default split is 12 portions of 1 cup each.
The actual calories and protein depend on the chicken parts, fat removal, extraction, and final volume. Strained bones, meat, and vegetables cannot be counted as if they were eaten.
This is the same store-bought reference used for the Cajun chicken pasta. No separate estimate is available for the untested clarified consommé variation.

directions.title: Blanch
directions.text: Put the chicken parts in a pot and cover with cold tap water. Bring to a boil, then boil hard for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse the chicken parts with tap water. Discard the blanching water.

directions.title: Load the cooker
directions.text: Put the chicken, vegetables, and seasoning into the Instant Pot. Add fresh water until the contents sit just shy of the pressure-cooking maximum fill line—4 quarts on my model. That's the final fill level with everything in the pot, not 4 quarts of added water.

directions.title: Pressure cook
directions.text: Cook on high pressure for 90 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally.

directions.title: Strain and store
directions.text: Strain out the solids. This usually gives me about 3 quarts, enough for three quart-size mason jars. Cool rapidly in shallow containers or an ice-water bath, then transfer to clean jars for refrigerated storage. Refrigerate for 3–4 days, or freeze for longer storage.

notes: One base batch yields about 96 fl oz / 3 quarts.
I tend to use necks and feet. Wings alone are fine if that's what you can find; flats and tips are better than drums.
I wouldn't suggest feet alone. Haven't established whether necks alone work well.
The 4-quart line is specific to my Instant Pot Pro. Follow your cooker's pressure-cooking fill limit. Scaling ingredients doesn't increase the cooker's capacity.
The 90 minutes is time at pressure; allow extra time for heating and natural pressure release.

Optional variations
Clarified consommé—not tried yet. Try Chris Young's chicken-breast/myosin clarification technique: blend stock with raw chicken breast, then pressure cook again and strain. Follow the linked demonstration starting at 11:53 for the complete method. Chicken quantity and second cooking time haven't been recorded here.
